CITY OF LA VERNE
Community Development Department

DATE:  November 1, 2022

TO:  Development Review Committee

FROM:  Gabriel Rivera, Assistant Planner

SUBJECT:  Case No. 128-22CL – Classification of Use regarding a Reiki therapy and meditation
  business within the Old Town Specific Plan Zone

AGENDA SUMMARY

On October 3, 2022, Michelle Cortez, the owner of Luna Healing and Wellness Studio, applied for
a Certificate of Use and Occupancy permit to move her business from her location at 2497 Foothill
Boulevard, Unit C to 2332 D Street, Suite D. The new location is located within the Historic Core
Retail sector of the Old Town La Verne Specific Plan. A Reiki therapy and meditation business is
not listed as a use within the Historic Core Retail sector, however, uses not classified may be
considered through the Classification of Use process.

Staff has reviewed the application and after reviewing the permitted, conditionally permitted, and
prohibited uses chart (Figure 9.3) of the Old Town La Verne Specific Plan, it was determined that
the use would function most similarly to a personal services use, which is considered a permitted
use within the Historic Core Retail sector.

The Development Review Committee (DRC) is asked to determine the permissibility of the
proposed use within the Historic Core Retail sector of the Old Town La Verne Specific Plan.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Development Review Committee consider the following:

  1. Classify the proposed Reiki therapy and meditation business within the Historic Core Retail
  sector of the Old Town La Verne Specific Plan as similar to a personal services use with a
  retail use component.

BACKGROUND

Michelle Cortez, owner of Luna Healing and Wellness, was originally located at 2497 Foothill
Boulevard, Unit C, which is located within the Foothill Boulevard Specific Plan and had been
approved at that location under a Conditional Use Permit in 2019. The business consisted of yoga
classes, individual Reiki healing therapy sessions, wellness coaching, and nutrition consultation.
Privately owned or operated sports and fitness clubs, such as the one that was proposed by Mrs.
Cortez, required a Conditional Use Permit for operation as required by the Foothill Boulevard
 Case No. 128-22CL – Luna Healing and Wellness Classification of Use
November 1, 2022
Page 2

Specific Plan due to the yoga component of the business. On November 13, 2019, the Planning
Commission had approved, under Resolution No. 1249, Mrs. Cortez’s proposal to operate her
business under a Conditional Use Permit (CUP). Mrs. Cortez operated her business at 2497
Foothill Boulevard, Unit C, for three years. Since her operation began in 2019, there have not been
any complaints received regarding the business operation.

Section 9 of the Oldtown La Verne Specific Plan includes a chart, Figure 9.3, which identifies the
permitted, nonpermitted, and conditional uses within each sector of the specific plan. Under the
Historic Core Retail section of the chart and based on the description provided by the applicant, it
was apparent to staff that the use described is not listed on the chart of uses, therefore requiring a
Classification of Use. In such cases where the use cannot be accurately determined in relation to
the Specific Plan, the Development Review Committee has the authority to determine the
permissibility of the proposed use according to Section 18.10.070 “Classification of Use” of the La
Verne Municipal Code. The section of the municipal code which applies Classification of Use is
included in Attachment B.

Proposal

In a narrative (Attachment C) submitted to staff, Mrs. Cortez describes her business operations as
a wellness studio, consisting of Reiki Healing therapy, intuitive life coaching, crystal healing
therapy, sound bath healing, meditation, along with a small retail component consisting of the sale
of crystals. The goal of Luna Healing and Wellness is to provide energy healing services which
help her clients improve their emotional, mental, and physical wellbeing. The applicant describes
Reiki Healing therapy as a holistic, noninvasive Japanese healing technique that has been
practiced for centuries. In a typical session, energy is channeled to the body to improve the flow of
energy and balance the chakras for healing. The intuitive life coaching service consists of a
coaching approach that uses emotional and spiritual healing methods to help clients break down
and address barriers in all areas of their life. The crystal healing therapy service is also a
noninvasive form of vibrational energy healing that involves the placement of crystals on the body,
which aides in cleansing and diffusing energy. These services are consistent with what was
originally proposed under the CUP for the applicant’s previous location, however the previous
location featured yoga fitness classes in addition to the above listed services. All services would
be conducted on site through appointment bookings, conducted as a one-on-one service, and each
booking typically lasts about an hour long. The business would operate on the weekdays from
11:00am to 8:00pm, Saturdays from 9:00am, and Sundays from 9:00am to 2:00pm. Mrs. Cortez
would be the only employee on site; however, she does plan on hiring more as the business grows.

Analysis

Utilizing Mrs. Cortez’s narrative describing the business operations proposed for the space at 2332
D Street, Suite D, staff reviewed the Old Town La Verne Specific Plan’s chart of permitted and
conditionally permitted uses to determine what type of classification could be given for Luna Healing
and Wellness. The chart below shows the various types of uses permitted in the Historic Core
Retail sector of the specific plan which most relate to the proposed use. After reviewing the chart
within the specific plan, staff determined that the most consistent use to what was proposed to the
applicant would be a personal services use, along with a retail use component. This is due to the
various types of services proposed by the applicant relate mainly to a service that directly involves
the client, similar to how a barber shop or beauty salon provides services that directly involve and
affect the client.
 Case No. 128-22CL – Luna Healing and Wellness Classification of Use

The Old Town La Verne Specific Plan, under section 9.4, states that: “All land uses not specifically
listed in this Specific Plan are prohibited, however the DRC may determine through the
Classification of Use process that any use not listed is comparable to a listed use and shall be
treated in a similar manner. Staff has prepared this report so that the Development Review
Committee may decide on the Classification of Use for Luna Healing and Wellness Studio.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act per Section 15301
(Class 1) and exempt per Section 15061(b)(3), as well as exempt from the La Verne Environmental
Guidelines. No further environmental review is required.
